record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: Let Γ = (V, E) be a continuous graph in which each edge is a unit-length continuous interval, and let α_r(Γ) denote the maximum size of an r-independent set, meaning a set I ⊆ E such that every two distinct points p, q ∈ I satisfy d(p, q) ≥ 2r. The paper asks for a structural and complexity classification of this problem: as a function of both the radius r > 0 and the structure of the underlying graph, for which cases can one compute α_r(Γ) in polynomial time, and for which cases is the problem NP-hard?

evidence.quote: Definition 9. Given a positive real number r > 0, a set of points I ⊆ E is called an r-independent (or r-stable) set of Γ if for any two points p, q ∈ I, it holds that d(p, q) ≥ 2r. The r-independence number of Γ, further referred as αr(Γ) or αr for simplicity, is the cardinality of the maximum r-independent set in Γ.

Clearly, the complexity of the problem is highly dependent not only on the nature of the number r but also on the specific structure of the graph. Thus, the open question of this section is to have a picture of such a joint dependency.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A continuous graph is a pair Γ = (V, E) where V is a finite set of vertices and E is a finite set of edges, each edge being modeled as a unit-length continuous interval whose two endpoints are identified with elements of V. The set E is endowed with the intrinsic shortest-path metric d, so that every point on every edge is treated as a point of the graph, and the distance d(p, q) between two such points is the length of a shortest path along the union of edges connecting them.

For a positive real number r > 0, a subset I ⊆ E (viewed as a set of points of the continuous graph) is called an r-independent set of Γ if for every two distinct points p, q ∈ I one has d(p, q) ≥ 2r. The r-independence number α_r(Γ) is defined as the supremum of |I| over all r-independent sets I of Γ.

Provide a complete structural and computational classification of the decision/optimization problem of computing α_r(Γ), as a function jointly of:
(i) the radius parameter r > 0 (e.g., r rational, irrational, fixed, or part of the input), and
(ii) the combinatorial structure of the underlying finite graph (V, E) (e.g., trees, planar graphs, bounded-degree graphs, bipartite graphs, general graphs, etc.).

Specifically, characterize precisely those combinations of r and graph class for which α_r(Γ) can be computed in polynomial time, and those for which the problem is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any work providing a joint structural/complexity classification of the r-independence number for continuous (metric) graphs as a function of r and the underlying graph class. The problem is posed as an open question in a recent survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs, and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Independent set (graph theory) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General background on independent sets; no discussion of r-independent sets in continuous/metric graphs with unit-length edges.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on independent sets do not address the continuous-graph r-independence variant, supporting that the joint complexity classification remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Interval Scheduling and Colorful Independent Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Independent sets in interval graphs are polynomial-time solvable, but the continuous-graph r-independence problem differs and is not classified here.
status_evidence.claim: No existing classification covers the r-independence problem on continuous graphs across all r and graph structures.
